title: Seven-storey rental building proposed on Fergus Avenue
subtitle: Committee also backed a townhouse rezoning in the Trussler West subdivision and asked staff to explore affordable units.
overview: The Planning and Strategic Initiatives Committee held public hearings on two development applications. Its decisions are recommendations that Council will consider later.

The main item was a proposal for a seven-storey rental building with 78 units at 142-146 Fergus Avenue. The committee recommended the Official Plan and zoning changes needed for it {{vote:m1}}. The plan includes a park block at the front of the site that would become city property. The committee added a direction for staff to work with the applicant on more density and possible affordable units, and to report back at the February 27, 2023 Council meeting. The Mayor declared a conflict and took no part.

The committee also recommended a zoning change for vacant blocks in the Trussler West subdivision {{vote:m2}}. It would allow street townhouses, with a total of 42 units. For residents, these decisions affect local housing supply, parkland, parking and the look of the neighbourhoods.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended adopting the Official Plan Amendment for 142-146 Fergus Avenue and forwarding it to the Region of Waterloo for approval.
The committee recommended approving the zoning by-law amendment for 142-146 Fergus Avenue, which enables the seven-storey rental building and a park block at the front of the site.
The committee recommended adopting the applicant's urban design brief and applying it through the site plan approval process.
Staff were directed to work with the applicant on possibly adding density and affordable units, and to report back at the February 27, 2023 Council meeting.
The committee recommended approving a zoning by-law amendment for vacant blocks in the Trussler West subdivision to allow street townhouses.

debate: Councillors liked the Fergus Avenue design and its location near transit, shops and parks. Several said rental housing and mid-rise intensification are needed. One said the city should be ready to accept growth if it wants to limit sprawl.

One councillor asked whether the applicant would add density in exchange for affordable units. The applicant's representative said extra units would likely mean less parking and noted that nearby buildings are low-rise. Staff said they had no major difficulty with the idea, but height, shadow and neighbour concerns would need review. The zoning already allows eight storeys.

Councillors asked about sustainability features, such as avoiding fossil fuel heating and using low-carbon materials. The applicant's representative said detailed design had not started and a sustainability statement could come with the site plan application.

On neighbour concerns, the applicant's representative said an angular plane analysis had been done for privacy and the ground floor has no homes. Staff said the traffic study found no concerns, though it did not look at left turns at the nearby corner.
The Trussler West item drew few questions. Staff confirmed that the site-specific provisions allow covered porches and terraces closer to the street than the general by-law would.
